meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I'm Meredith Kalinowski. I'm Owen's mother, and I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct. Why does my son have a zero, Hale, and why did he learn it from a gradebook on his phone in the middle of class?
I didn't come for thanks, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn and an apology for how he learned of it, and if that does not happen I will take this to the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal's review if she doesn't get them.
What moved her: Nothing, because you gave her no document or answer to weigh.
What cost ground: Answering her first question with a thank-you and no answer about who decided or whether Owen was heard, which left her sure the zero came first and the questions after.
Try next time: After her opening question, say in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her and that this was wrong, then put a dated document on the table.
